readthrough.heading: Measured tape, conditional narrative
readthrough.title: What the completed session can and cannot show
readthrough.body: Across these twelve companies, the daily bars establish price, range and volume for October 30. The research log records no verified company-specific event for this edition; Monday earnings and later filings will test the investment cases.

headline: Friday October 30 close: broad AI risk repricing, with Intel and AI infrastructure under pressure
quick: All twelve tracked stocks closed lower on October 30; the largest measured declines were INTC -28.5761%, HOOD -7.2060% and PLTR -6.2672%.
INTC volume was 454,221,300 shares versus a 98,370,530 trailing average; NVDA volume was 168,039,400 versus 99,407,925. Volume confirms participation, not cause.

macro.dd: The twelve company moves below come solely from validated completed Twelve Data daily bars. Earnings and macro releases provide dated context, but a headline does not prove the cause of a measured move.

entries.happened: AAPL closed the completed October 30, 2026 NYSE session at $344.63, -1.23% versus the prior close of $348.91. The session ranged from $334.35 to $349.19, with volume of 67,797,500 shares versus a trailing average of 38,682,545. No verified company-specific event was found for AAPL in the dated sources checked for this edition.
entries.why: The measured down move is evidence about trading, not a diagnosis of the business. For AAPL, the next investment test is whether operating results, cash generation, competitive position and valuation support the share price as rates and AI capital spending evolve. Volume relative to its trailing average provides a participation check, but it cannot identify who traded or why. The October 30 tape should be tested against subsequent filings, guidance and follow-through rather than treated as proof of causation.

analysis.heading: Operating evidence that matters next
analysis.body: The next useful evidence for AAPL is a dated company release, filing or earnings disclosure that updates revenue, margins, cash generation, demand or capacity. Compare that evidence with management commitments and the valuation already reflected in the stock before treating one completed session as a lasting change in business value. If dated evidence persists in guidance and later margins, the investment case changes; if not, the move may remain a positioning event.
